Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team found the latency and cost numbers helpful. As we prepare for procurement, a few security questions came up from our InfoSec team about Redwood's default data handling that I wasn't able to get answers to from the docs:

- For the Hosted API, are the original prompts (user inputs) and the generated outputs stored by Redwood by default? If so, what is the default retention window?
- Are request/response pairs treated differently from other logs (e.g., telemetry, metrics)?
- Is there a per-request opt-out or a per-account default setting to avoid storing prompts/outputs? We may want ephemeral processing for some flows.
- If we request deletion, what is the path and SLAs (e.g., purge within X hours/days)?

Can you point us to a concise matrix or summarize the defaults? Attaching our standard checklist.

Appreciate it — we need this for the security review next week.

Hi Amanda — thanks for the concise list. Summary below (short version first), and I attached a small matrix that maps "what" to "default retention" and deletion paths. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through.

Short summary (Hosted API):
- Prompts (request inputs) and outputs (model completions) are retained by default for 30 days to support abuse detection, quality monitoring, and debugging.
- Telemetry/metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) are retained in aggregated form for 90 days; low-level traces used for incident triage are kept for 30 days.
- Embeddings: raw input used to generate embeddings is retained for 30 days; the produced vector embeddings used in persistent index are controlled by your app (Redwood does not automatically index customer embeddings).
- Opt-out: per-request opt-out is available for Hosted customers via the X-Redwood-No-Store: 1 header and as a tenant-level setting in the Console (requires account owner).
- Deletion: we offer a deletion job (Delete API and Console delete workflow). For Hosted API default accounts, deletion requests are processed within 72 hours; account-wide purge for all stored prompts/outputs will be marked for background purge and fully removed within 7 days.

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private:
- Hosted: defaults above (30 / 90 days); opt-out header supported.
- Dedicated: default configuration is 90 days for logs/telemetry but prompts/outputs retention can be set at contract time; Dedicated customers can request shorter windows or an automatic purge schedule.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): retention policy is customer-controlled; Redwood control plane does not retain customer PII/requests unless explicitly enabled.

Scope clarifications:
- "Prompts" = what is supplied in the request's input/text field.
- "Outputs" = the model's completion/generation.
- Session keys, ephemeral KV caches, and in-memory runtime caches are not persisted to disk across requests.
- Attachments passed as part of request metadata are stored only if explicitly uploaded to our storage APIs and will follow object storage retention settings.

Next steps: I've attached a matrix (data-retention-matrix.xlsx) and a DPA summary that highlights contractual retention options. If Acme needs shorter windows for hosted traffic, we can scope that into the DPA or recommend Dedicated with a custom purge schedule.

2) If we start with Hosted and later move to Dedicated, will prior Hosted prompts/outputs be preserved unless we explicitly request purge? We need to ensure migration does not unintentionally keep historical chat transcripts.

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on what Redwood stores by default

Hi Amanda — quick answers:

1) X-Redwood-No-Store: 1 is honored for chat, completions, and embeddings endpoints. Practically speaking:
   - The header prevents storing request/response payloads (prompts & outputs) in persistent logs.
   - Aggregated billing/usage counters and non-identifying telemetry (token counts, latency histograms) are still retained for billing and SLO/operational monitoring. We can provide aggregated telemetry reports without exposing raw text.

2) Migration from Hosted -> Dedicated: historical Hosted data remains in Hosted storage unless you request a purge prior to migration. We will not automatically migrate customer-hosted prompts/outputs into Dedicated storage. If you want a clean cutover, we recommend raising a Hosted purge job via the Console before switching routing.

Deletion evidence / audit proof: we provide a purge report (JSON) that lists job id, affected buckets, and timestamps once background purge completes. For enterprise deals we can add a signed audit statement as part of the DPA addendum. Standard Hosted purge evidence appears in the Console audit log and is exported as a time-stamped report; SLA for processing is 72 hours and background removal within 7 days as Tessa noted.

If you'd like, I'll schedule a focused 30-minute call with our security engineering lead to walk through logs, sample purge reports, and an example DPA clause.

- Vivek
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
